# Full-precision recompute of the four 2026-09-24 wall artifacts (task #26)
# Generated by audit.py in this directory from the .json/.txt files beside ../ ;
# nothing here is a new measurement. 2026-09-25.

## 0. Why the stdout could not carry these claims

  The bench prints one decode arm as `decode  64 tok in 2.71 s  23.6 tok/s`.
  Two lossy fields, two ways to get ms/token, and the artifacts used both:

    from the seconds field  step = 0.01 s / 64 tok          = 0.156 ms/token, always
    from the rate field     step = 1000/(r-0.05) - 1000/(r+0.05), rate-dependent:
                                r =   14.1 tok/s -> 0.503 ms/token
                                r =   20.4 tok/s -> 0.240 ms/token
                                r =   20.9 tok/s -> 0.229 ms/token
                                r =   23.6 tok/s -> 0.180 ms/token
                                r =   28.4 tok/s -> 0.124 ms/token
                                r =  149.7 tok/s -> 0.004 ms/token
                                r =  448.0 tok/s -> 0.000 ms/token

  So a quoted `42.37` from 23.6 tok/s is really 42.37 +/- 0.09, and a quoted
  `70.92` from 14.1 tok/s is really 70.92 +/- 0.25. Three consequences show up
  below: two runs that printed the SAME value were not equal, one published
  difference was smaller than its own quantum, and one pre-registered admission
  band was drawn at the quantized edge.

   PUBLISHED                                          FULL PRECISION       VERDICT
   ratio 0.792/0.793/0.796, median 0.793             0.7915/0.7934/0.7960   holds
   allpaka decode spread 1.013x                      1.012864x    holds
   llama decode spread 1.010x                        1.009481x    holds

   The 6.1 is not a ms/token gap: 29.5949 - 23.4258 = 6.169 is the
   TOK/S difference of pair 1, printed to 2 dp and then given a time's unit.
   The same pair's gap in ms/token is 42.6881 - 33.7896 = 8.8985, and across
   the three in-band pairs it is 8.629-8.898 (median 8.853).
   The `13` it was contrasted with IS a ms/token figure: the recorded 0.72x
   row of the status table, read against llama's own median, is 13.14 ms/token of
   gap (46.93 - 33.79), so that sentence set a real time against a rate
   difference and understated the live gap by 31%.

   Nothing downstream of it changes sign: 12.6 ms/token outside the kernel sum
   is still 1.4x the 8.9 ms llama gap (not 2.0x the 6.1 ms one), so `attribute
   the residue before re-opening the q3_k chain` was already the right order,
   and the residue is a somewhat smaller prize relative to the gap than
   published. The 1.700x was real but belongs to best-clean-over-worst-rejected
   (23.639/13.909), not to the three rejected arms, which span 1.12x.

### 2.2 section 8.1, the bracketed series (P(experts)=20.6, P(qkv)=8.4, P(all)=30.3)

   brackets `42.55 / 42.37 / 42.37 / 70.92 / 42.37 / 43.86`   42.5258 / 42.3980 / 42.3998 / 70.8020 / 42.3503 / 43.8977
     -> the three brackets printed identically as 42.37 are 42.3503 / 42.3980 / 42.3998,
        span 0.0495 ms - inside one 0.156 ms quantum of the seconds field,
        so the printed equality was rounding, not agreement. The four in-cluster brackets
        (r1-r3, qkv) span 0.1755 ms; 8.2's `42.37-43.86 = 3.5%` band is really
        42.3503-43.8977 = 3.65%. `tightest bracket all day` in the split
        artifact is the same effect, there of 0.049 ms.
   r4 bracket 70.92                                70.8020         WRONG (1000/14.1 vs
                                                                     1000/14.123896)
   saves 27.42/27.27/+11.60/-/+7.16/+41.63           +27.3866 / +27.2810 / +11.6118 / +55.0084 / +7.1161 / +41.6654
   R 1.33/1.32/-/-/0.85/1.37                         1.3294 / 1.3243 / 0.5637 / 2.6703 / 0.8472 / 1.3751   r3/r4 are the REJECTED
                                                      pairs, so their R is printed
                                                      but not used; on the clean
                                                      ones the >=1.20 format-specific
                                                      branch fires with more margin
                                                      than printed (1.3294 / 1.3243 / 0.8472).
   `saves reproduce to 0.15 ms` (r1 vs r2)          0.1056 ms   holds, tighter
   `the six baselines spread 60.2% (42.37-70.92)`  full precision 67.18% all six,
                                                      3.65% excluding r4. Even the
                                                      quantized numbers it cites give
                                                      67.38%, not 60.2%: ARITHMETIC WRONG in every
                                                      reading. The 8% gate trips either way.
   `GPU-executing agrees with the wall save to       0.152 / 0.172 / 0.096 / 0.180 / 0.069 / 0.369
    within 0.1 ms`                                   ms - the two experts pairs are 0.15-0.17,
                                                     the `all` pair 0.37.  OVERSTATED.

     The disagreement is exactly the change in the non-executing residue
     (wall - executing), and the GPU clock splits that residue into
     scheduling + idle and a remainder outside the counters:
     pair          brk residue  arm residue   = sched+idle brk/arm  + rest brk/arm   diff
     experts r1        0.7758      0.6236   =  0.2344/0.1719  +  0.5414/0.4517   0.1522
     experts r2        0.7261      0.5545   =  0.2031/0.1406  +  0.5230/0.4139   0.1716
     qkv               0.7097      0.6404   =  0.1875/0.1875  +  0.5222/0.4529   0.0693
     all               0.6789      0.3104   =  0.1406/0.0938  +  0.5383/0.2166   0.3685
   The last column is the |wall save - executing save| of the table above, to the
   microsecond - it is an identity, not a second measurement. A removal arm has
   less residue than its own baseline (fewer waits to overlap, less host work
   outside the counters), so the wall save is systematically the larger number.
   What survives is the direction and the size: two independent clocks agree on
   the experts save to 0.15-0.17 ms on 27 ms, and on the `all` save to 0.37 on
   41.7 - which is not the `within 0.1 ms` 8.2 claims, and 8.2's use of that
   agreement to argue the saves are not scheduling artifacts is weakened
   accordingly (the argument still holds at 0.6% of the effect).

### 2.3 section 9.1 / Amendment 3 - the threshold that moves

   pair        bracket    arm      save     e(bracket)  e(arm)   census P   R
   attend r1     42.3562  41.5494  0.8068    41.6406  40.9375      0.00      n/a
   head r1       42.4215  41.5414  0.8801    41.7031  40.8750      1.10   0.8001
   head r2       75.9089  59.5358 16.3731   REJECTED (bracket left the cluster)
   attend r2     42.4533  95.8058 -53.3525   REJECTED (bracket left the cluster)
   head r3       51.8638  47.6892  4.1747   REJECTED (bracket left the cluster)
   attend r3     52.7159  55.3270 -2.6112   REJECTED (bracket left the cluster)

   published attend 0.88 + head 0.88 = 1.76 ms, `0.06 ABOVE the 1.7 threshold,
   so neither branch fires cleanly`.  Full precision: 0.8068 + 0.8801 =
   1.6869 ms, which is 0.0131 ms BELOW it. The pre-registered `<= 1.7
   combined` branch - `the Amendment 2 decomposition is wrong and the group
   guards come under suspicion` - is the one that fires.

   How to hold that: the flip is 0.0131 ms on a one-pair measurement whose own
   bracket (42.3562) sits 0.0138 ms UNDER the 42.37 floor of the admission cluster
   that Amendment 3 drew from quantized values (`a pair whose bracket leaves the
   42.37-42.55 cluster is reported but not used for ratios`). Read literally at
   full precision, that rule excludes the attend pair it was applied to - one
   of the two arms the threshold is computed from. So the honest statement is
   that the 1.7/3.5 fork does not discriminate at this resolution, not that the
   guards are now under suspicion. What does not move either way: both saves
   are 0.81/0.88 ms against 1.3 predicted for head+router, head's R = 0.800 is
   inside +-30%, and attend's unpriced line is real but small.

   qkv                                     published  7.16   7.1161
   attend                                  published  0.88   0.8068
   head                                    published  0.88   0.8801
   ---- sum of single-group removals       published 36.20   36.1369
   e - sum                                 published  5.50   5.6131
   floor (exec with every group skipped)   published  1.92   1.9219
   => interaction term                     published  3.58   3.6913  = 8.84% of e
   reference wall = median of the three in-cluster brackets  42.3980 ms/token
   gap against the census 30.12                              12.2780  (published 12.25)
   term                                              published   full precision   share
   K-quant expert inflation (mean experts save - 20.60)     +6.68        +6.7338     54.8%
   inter-kernel interaction (9.2)                           +3.58        +3.6913     30.1%
   unpriced floor, norms/bars/sampling/lm_head              +1.92        +1.9219     15.7%
   unpriced attention-over-KV line                          +0.88        +0.8068      6.6%
   qkv cheaper in situ than at micro rate (save - 8.40)     -1.24        -1.2839    -10.5%
   head cheaper than its census price (save - 1.10)         -0.22        -0.2199     -1.8%
   wall outside the GPU busy interval (median)              +0.67        +0.7179      5.8%
   ---- total                                            +12.27       +12.3679
   closure against the gap: +0.0899 ms (published claimed +0.02)

     Term by term against the published 9.3 block: K-quant expert inflation
     27.334 - 20.60 = +6.734 (published +6.68), interaction +3.691 (published +3.58),
     floor +1.922 (published +1.92), attention line +0.807 (published +0.88), qkv
     7.116 - 8.40 = -1.284 (published -1.24), head 0.880 - 1.10 = -0.220 (published -0.22),
     wall outside GPU busy +0.718 (published +0.67). The largest single term move is
     0.111 ms (the interaction term) and no share changes band.
     The residue question stays answered the way the artifact
     answered it: experts inflate, ~3.7 ms is scheduling interaction, ~1.9 ms
     is an unpriced floor, ~0.8 ms is attention over KV.

## 3. 2026-09-24-30b-skip-control/results.txt

   section 2 `baseline 148.5-149.9 tok/s (6.66-6.91 ms/token)`: the 18 baselines
   are 144.6535-150.2102 tok/s =
   6.6573-6.9131 ms/token, median 6.6790. The ms range published
   is right; the tok/s range is not, and it hides the one outlier the text
   then discusses (r3 attend's bracket is 144.6535 tok/s, not 148.5).

   arm       P(ms)    brackets r1 / r2 / r3              saves r1 / r2 / r3            R pub   R full
   all      4.92  6.6974 / 6.6737 / 6.7506   5.9535 / 5.9233 / 5.9803    1.21   1.2101
   experts  2.88  6.6860 / 6.6573 / 6.6908   2.9459 / 2.9090 / 2.9416    1.02   1.0214
   qkv      1.34  6.6764 / 6.6898 / 6.6785   1.5722 / 1.5832 / 1.5767    1.18   1.1766
   head      0.7  6.7319 / 6.6713 / 6.6813   0.5313 / 0.4697 / 0.5039    0.72   0.7198
   router    0.1  6.6722 / 6.6637 / 6.6760   -6.9799 / -6.8849 / -6.9414  -69.48 -69.4139
   attend    n/a  6.6794 / 6.6777 / 6.9131   0.3664 / 0.3961 / 0.5356       -      n/a

   The fork's evidence (q4_k experts do NOT inflate, R = 1.02) holds to three
   digits (1.0214), and so does every other arm. The brackets that printed as
   6.68 / 6.66 / 6.69 for experts are 6.6860 / 6.6573 / 6.6908;
   the three `all` brackets printed 6.70 / 6.68 / 6.75 and are 6.6974 / 6.6737 /
   6.7506. At this scale the stdout quantum is 0.0045 ms/token, so the 30B
   tables are the ones the quantization did NOT damage - which is exactly why
   they were usable as the control.

   section 6 `sum of parts 5.38 vs all 5.95, extra 0.57 ms`: full precision
   5.4182 vs 5.9535 -> extra 0.5352 ms = 8.48% of the 30B's own
   executing time (6.3125 ms/token), not 8.6%. The cross-model claim in the
   differential's 9.2 (`the identical ratio, both models the same percentage`)
   is 8.84% on the 235B and 8.48% here: same order, not identical, and
   both still inside the `a removal probe under-counts by ~8-9%` rule, which
   survives as the rule it was read as.

## 4. 2026-09-24-235b-decode-split/results.txt

   section 1, the plain/split pairs
   rep  plain ms     split ms    delta     delta%   published      plain sched  split sched  plain enc  split enc
     1    42.3435    48.9924   6.6489   15.70   42.37/49.02/+6.65        0.0781       0.4844     0.4375     1.8438

     3    42.3174    91.9666  49.6492  117.33   42.37/58.72/rejected        0.0625       0.0938     0.4531     1.8594

   - `All three plain brackets read exactly 42.37 ms/token (23.60 tok/s), the
     tightest bracket this model has given all day`: the three plain arms are
     42.3435 / 42.2941 / 42.3174 ms/token. Not equal - equal to the 0.156 ms
     quantum of the seconds field they were read from. It is still the tightest
     bracket of the day (0.0494 ms, vs 0.1755 ms for the four in-cluster b2
     baselines, 0.0495 ms for the three that printed 42.37, and 1.4750 ms for the t3
     trial here), so the claim survives with
     the word `exactly` removed.
   - rep 3's split arm is published at 58.72 ms/token. The artifact reads
     91.9666 ms/token (10.873517 tok/s, JSON median identical to the
     `decode 64 tok in 5.89 s` line). 58.72 appears nowhere in r3-split; the
     rejection stands on the prefill
     (97.2 tok/s against 206.0/195.5/199.3 in the plain arms) and on its own
     GPU-executing time (89.750 ms/token vs 41.7/41.6/41.6 in plain), but the number
     quoted for it in the write-up is not the number measured.
   - `host encode 1.84 ms/token in both`: plain is
     0.4375 / 0.4531 ms/token, split 1.8438 / 1.8438. The encode step from
     the extra per-stage encoders is +1.4062 ms/token host-side, which is part of the
     +5.5-6.6 ms this section prices, and `in both` hid it.

   section 5.1/5.5, the barrier arms (s1, s2 and the fully bracketed t3-t5)
   pair          bracket     arm       delta      published delta    e-brk/e-arm
   s1 barf         47.7413   47.9249    0.1837            +0.16    45.594/45.719
   s1 bar          47.9946   48.1516    0.1569            +0.16    45.812/45.953

   t3 bases 47.7556-49.2306 (1.4750)  barf 49.0951 (+1.0488)  bar 47.7934 (-0.2529)
   t4 bases 47.7342-47.9782 (0.2440)  barf 47.7425 (-0.0245)  bar 47.7699 (+0.0028)

   - 5.1 publishes both clean s1 deltas as +0.16. Full precision: barf +0.1837,
     bar +0.1569. Both brackets and both arms are ~0.2 ms slower than the
     published table says, and the two deltas are not the same number.
   - 5.5 publishes t3 as `47.81-49.22 (1.41)` with arms 49.06/47.81; the
     artifact is 47.7556-49.2306 (1.4750) with arms 49.0951 (barf) and
     47.7934 (bar). t3's bar arm is below all three of its own baselines,
     which is the degrading-window signature 5.2 used to reject s2 - t3 is
     softer evidence than published, not firmer.
   - 5.5 publishes t4 as `47.66-47.97 (0.31)`. The three t4 baselines are
     47.7342 / 47.9782 / 47.7671 (0.2440 ms wide), i.e. t4 is cleaner than
     published and 47.66 is not in the artifact. The two arms are
     47.7425 (barf) and 47.7699 (bar), both under the median baseline 47.7671
     - consistent with the null.
   - t5 is in the directory but not in the write-up: bases
     47.6930 / 48.3079 / 47.8433, barf 47.7300, bar 47.7379. Its bracket is
     0.6148 ms wide, so its range is inside the published `0.31 ms trial`
     rule only if that rule is read as `t4 alone`, but both of its arms are the
     two fastest runs of the trial, which is 5.2's rejection signature. Read
     against the median baseline t5 gives barf -0.1133 and bar
     -0.1054 ms - the same size as s1's +0.16/+0.18 but the other
     sign, i.e. inside the trial's own noise either way, so it corroborates the
     null (5.5's `n=2 independent clean trials` is really 3 trials: t4 strictly
     inside its own 0.31 ms rule, t3 and t5 wider but pointing the same way, both
     arms at the quiet end) and does not disturb section 5.4's verdict,
     which rests on the per-label `down` prices, not on the wall.

   section 5.6, the qkv control
   k1: bases 48.4402 / 106.5885 (spread 58.1483), arm 37.5099   published 48.44 / 106.56, 58.12, 37.50

     (published 7.03). Arms: k1 37.5099 (37.50), k2 44.9967 (45.00). All inside
     0.01 ms of the published table - the control passes at full precision.

### 4.5 a third instrument the artifacts already had: the coarse phase table in the JSON

   Every bench JSON carries .measurements[decode].phases - per-subsystem totals
   for the whole 64-token window, at full float. In split mode those are
   experts / qkv / attention / norm / router / other; the write-ups quoted only
   the fine stdout label table. The two disagree, systematically:

   run         wall     phases   residual | coarse experts  qkv  attention  norm  router  other
   r1-split    48.9924  44.0020    4.9904 |   28.3753 5.2403    5.2202 2.4669  1.7094 0.9898
   r2-split    47.8317  44.0259    3.8058 |   28.4426 5.2438    5.2300 2.5017  1.7103 0.8975
   s1-bar      48.1516  44.2206    3.9310 |   28.4549 5.3347    5.3187 2.4587  1.7494 0.9042
   s1-barf     47.9249  44.0013    3.9236 |   28.4557 5.2518    5.2410 2.4604  1.7216 0.8708
   t3-bar      47.7934  44.0009    3.7925 |   28.4194 5.2479    5.2297 2.4541  1.7183 0.9316
   t4-bar      47.7699  43.9812    3.7887 |   28.4199 5.2441    5.2370 2.5254  1.7208 0.8341
   t4-barf     47.7425  43.8970    3.8456 |   28.3946 5.2329    5.2153 2.5014  1.7199 0.8328
   t4-base1    47.7342  43.9639    3.7703 |   28.3978 5.2437    5.2239 2.4631  1.7200 0.9154
   t5-bar      47.7379  44.0155    3.7223 |   28.4114 5.2457    5.2306 2.4547  1.7082 0.9648

   - Section 1's printed rep-1 table (`experts 28.4 / qkv 5.2 / attention 5.2 /
     norm 2.5 / router 1.7 / other 1.0 / unaccounted 5.0 = 10.2%`) is confirmed
     by the JSON to the digit: it was read at good precision. The unaccounted
     line is 4.9904 ms/token here, i.e. 10.2% of the wall - the published
     10.2% is right, and section 5.4's `1.7-1.8 ms/token residual` is a
     different base (fine labels vs GPU-executing), not this one.
   - Coarse group against the fine labels it aggregates, same run (r1-split):
       coarse group     coarse    fine labels   coarse - fine
       experts          28.3753 (gate_up+down+swiglu+combine)    28.135    +0.2403
       qkv               5.2403        (qkv)     5.127    +0.1133
       attention         5.2202  (attend+wo)     5.065    +0.1552
       norm              2.4669    (resnorm)     2.441    +0.0259
       router            1.7094     (router)     1.709    +0.0004
       other             0.9898 (head+argmax)     0.996    -0.0062
     Every byte group is higher in the coarse table (+0.2403
     ms/token at the extreme on experts) and the small ones match to <0.01; the sums
     are 43.473 (fine, from 3-dp stdout) against 44.0020 (coarse, from JSON), a
     gap of +0.5290 ms/token = 1.20% of the coarse total. That is the
     MAX_SPLIT_SAMPLES = 2048 truncation of 5.4's caveat operating not by zeroing a
     label but by shaving ~1% off the fine sums - so a fine-label price is a
     LOWER bound. Scaling every fine label by the missing 1.22% puts the q3_k `down`
     stage's ratio to its census price at 2.12x rather than 2.09x. Distributing the
     gap by group instead - the experts carrying their own 0.85% shortfall -
     lands one quantum away at 2.11x. Either way the reading is
     `a shade over 2.1x`, not a new number. The
     per-stage conclusions do not move; the residual that should be quoted for
     unlabelled time is wall minus coarse (4.990 ms/token here), not the 1.7-1.8
     published from the fine table.
   - Both skip controls check out in the coarse table at full precision:
     k1 qkv-skip: coarse qkv 5.2942 -> absent (0.0000) and attention
     5.2822 -> 0.8424 ms/token - the qkv guard takes wo with it, which is
     what the fine table's two zeroed labels already said; experts
     28.4564 -> 28.4230, i.e. the expert group does NOT absorb the removed
     time. 5.6's control passes on the third instrument too.
     c1 head-skip: coarse other 0.9516 -> absent, so head lives in
     `other` and its 0.000 is a real skip. Its experts line reads
     34.6280 -> 31.0901, a 3.5379 ms/token drop that has nothing to
     do with head: c1 is a degraded-window pair
     (55.51/49.84 ms/token against
     the 47.7-48.2 clean split cluster), and in a degraded window every group is
     inflated. 5.3 used the fine labels of that pair as the clean-value control,
     and the fine values it quotes are clean relative to each other, but the
     absolute inflation is why the head control is weaker than k1 - which is
     exactly why 5.6 added k1.

## 5. Net effect on the published record
   DECISION-CHANGING (fix in place):
     1. e2e gap to llama: 8.85 ms/token median, not 6.1. 6.1 is a tok/s
        difference wearing a ms/token unit. Everything sized off `the gap to
        close` on this model inherits it.
     2. skip-differential 8.2: the six-baseline spread is 67.2%, not 60.2%,
        and the three brackets printed `42.37` are 42.3503-42.3998. The 8% gate
        trips by more than published; the per-pair defence it argues for is
        unchanged.
     3. skip-differential 9.1: attend+head = 1.687 ms, which is under the
        pre-registered 1.7 threshold, not 0.06 over it. Neither branch is
        credited at this resolution - see 2.3.
     4. decode-split 1: rep 3's rejected split arm is 91.97 ms/token, not 58.72.
   SIZED, NOT MOVED:
     5. R(experts) 1.32 -> 1.314 unbracketed, 1.329/1.324 bracketed;
        R(qkv) 0.85 -> 0.847; R(all) 1.37 -> 1.375. The format-specific
        branch holds with more margin than published (its floor was 1.20).
     6. 30B control: R = 1.2101 / 1.0214 / 1.1766 / 0.7198 against published
        1.21 / 1.02 / 1.18 / 0.72. The control's whole point survives.
     7. The 9.3 allocation moves by at most 0.111 ms per term and still closes
        on the gap (+0.0899 ms); the two-model interaction ratio is
        8.84% / 8.48%, not `identical`.
     8. decode-split 5.4's truncation caveat has a magnitude now: the fine label
        table sums 0.529 ms/token (= 1.20% of the coarse
        total) below the phase
        table of the same run and is low on every byte group, so a fine-label price
        is a lower bound. The `down` 2.09x becomes 2.12x;
        no conclusion in that artifact moves.
   INSTRUMENT RULE THIS AUDIT ESTABLISHES:
     Never derive ms/token from the bench stdout. The seconds field quantizes
     at 0.01 s / TG and the rate field at 0.05 tok/s, which at the 2026-09-24
     235B rates is 0.156 and 0.18-0.25 ms/token - the same size as the
     smallest effects those artifacts claim (barrier delta 0.157-0.184,
     baseline-cluster width 0.175). ALLPAKA_BENCH_REPORT writes
     .measurements[].summary.median at full float; every paired statistic in
     a new artifact must be computed from it, and an admission band must be
     stated in the same precision it will be tested at.
